---
title: Quantile
description: "A number represented by its position in the learned training distribution."
---

`Quantile` represents a number by its position in the learned training
distribution. For a payment dataset, it can express how an amount such as
`84.50` ranks among the training amounts. The example below uses that
representation to predict a later dispute. It offers an alternative to
[Number](number.qmd)'s magnitude representation; compare them on the same
held-out task.

```python
import relflow as rf

model = rf.Model.xs(
    amount=rf.Quantile,
    merchant=rf.Category,
    disputed=rf.Boolean(mask=True),
)
```

One labeled payment:

```yaml
amount: 84.50
merchant: North Market
disputed: false
```

Use `rf.Quantile(mask=True)` to predict a number through this representation.
Predictions return to the original units, within the learned numeric range.
The distribution belongs to this field across its training observations; it
is not automatically a separate amount distribution for each merchant.

## Input and representation

The Arrow leaf accepts integers and floating-point scalars; Booleans,
strings, and lists are rejected. NaN and infinity take the `other`
[value state](index.qmd#value-state) and do not enter the learned distribution
or numeric reconstruction loss. Put repeated measurements
inside a [Branch](branch.qmd). Nulls remain separate from numeric values;
unused branch slots are padded.

Each field learns its own approximate distribution from pristine training
values, including values selected as hidden reconstruction targets. Encoding
preserves source values as float64 before mapping them to float32 percentile
coordinates. The embedder combines the percentile and its Fourier features
with value state. The input representation does not retain a separate
magnitude lane: two amounts beyond the learned maximum both have percentile
`1`, even if their source values differ.

Equal values receive equal coordinates. A constant training distribution maps
its observed value to `0.5`. Values below the learned minimum map to `0`; values
above the learned maximum map to `1`. Before any finite training value has been
observed, numeric inputs use `0.5`.

## Options

| Option | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `compression` | `100` | Integer at least `10`; controls the detail retained by the approximate distribution summary. |
| `n_bands` | `8` | Positive number of Fourier frequencies; frequency `k` is `k * pi`, for `k` from `1` through `n_bands`. |
| `objective` | `"mae"` | Reconstruction loss in percentile units: `"mae"`, `"mse"`, or `"huber"`. |

[Shared leaf options](index.qmd#shared-leaf-options)
control masking, decoder pooling, and exported embeddings. Quantile does not
accept a `jitter` option.

## Learned state and output

Only consumed training batches update the learned distribution. Preparing or
prefetching a batch does not update it. Validation, test, and prediction reuse
the learned state. Repeated training presentations count again; nulls and
padding do not contribute. Checkpoints preserve the distribution.

RelFlow keeps a weighted-centroid t-digest in Arrow data rather than retaining
training rows. This is RelFlow's implementation, not PyArrow's native t-digest
kernel. Compression controls approximation detail, not a guaranteed percentile
error bound.

For an application-supplied trained `model`:

```python
normalization = rf.Quantile.normalization(
    model, rf.Address("amount")
)
```

The snapshot contains `count`, `compression`, `minimum`, `median`, and `maximum`.
The last three values are `None` until the field has observed numeric training
data. A [preprocessor](../guides/preprocessing.qmd) can pass its supplied
`encoding_context` in place of `model` to inspect the same field state.

Prediction `content` is a nullable `float64` scalar in source units. It is null
until a distribution has been learned. The decoder predicts a percentile in
`[0, 1]` and maps it back through the learned distribution, so numeric
predictions stay between the learned minimum and maximum. MAE and RMSE
metrics use source units; the reconstruction objective uses percentile units.
Source-unit error metrics are omitted until
the field has learned a distribution. Read the scalar alongside `state` and
`inferred` in the [prediction envelope](../reference/prediction-output.qmd).

These percentiles describe the numeric representation. They are not prediction
intervals or coverage estimates.

The [regression evidence](../evidence/quantile/rank-regression.html) measures held-out
learning against shuffled inputs. The
[extrapolation evidence](../evidence/quantile/clipped-extrapolation.html) measures the
error imposed by the learned support boundary.
The [representation tradeoff evidence](../evidence/quantile/representation-tradeoffs.html)
compares Number and Quantile under contaminated inputs and distinguishes
percentile-loss predictions from source-unit conditional means and medians.
